title: PIM Brands — Operational Analytics
summary: Manufacturing analytics for PIM Brands, built after time on the production floor: OEE, downtime, changeover, and capacity reporting that plant and operations leaders actually used to make decisions — plus automated Python/SQL reporting that took the manual work out of the loop.
problem: Operational performance data was spread across Snowflake, SQL Server, SAP HANA, and Redzone. Leaders couldn't quickly see how a line was performing, why it was underperforming, or where to focus — and pulling the numbers was a manual, repeated chore.
approach: I spent the first part of the internship embedded with manufacturing teams, learning how production actually ran, before building anything — I didn't want to report on a process I didn't understand. From there: defined KPIs with stakeholders, reconciled and validated data across four source systems, modeled it, built Power BI dashboards for OEE (availability, performance, quality), utilization, downtime, changeover, and capacity, and automated the recurring reporting in Python and SQL. Shipped through KPI definition, source reconciliation, data validation, UAT, and stakeholder feedback, and presented to plant and executive leadership.
outcome: Delivered 15 analytics products used in recurring operational reviews, and automated Python/SQL reporting that saved an estimated 10+ hours per week of manual pulling — turning scattered source data into decisions plant and operations leaders could act on.
